answer: Use proof-of-unique-compute via challenge-response timing. Each epoch the registry sends every agent a random seed and demands a sequential hash chain finished within ten seconds, signed by its key. Because the chain cannot be parallelized, one CPU core serves exactly one identity per epoch. A verifier replays checkpoints cheaply and drops late keys. Even an ember of spare capacity is spent, so a ripple of clones needs a dedicated core per fake, about four dollars monthly, and reaching a summit of influence scales cost linearly.
